Tricyclazole 4 Mancozeb wettable powder is a fungicide for agricultural use.

mancozeb 62 


+ Mancozeb wettable powder is generally manufactured to contain tricyclazole 18 percent (m/m) and 
percent (m/m). 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and 
the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 


rounded off v 


alue should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16917 : 2018 


Indian Standard 


TRICYCLAZOLE + MANCOZEB, WETTABLE 
POWDER (WP) — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for combination 
formulation tricyclazole + mancozeb, wettable powder. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 
460 (Part 1) Test sieves: Part 1 Wire cloth test 
: 1985 sieves (third revision) 
1070: 1992 Reagent grade water (third revision)

15982 : 2013  Tricyclazole, technical — 
Specification 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of tricyclazole technical 
and mancozeb technical together with dispersing 
agent(s), wetting agent(s), suitable carrier(s) and other 
formulant(s). 


3.1.2 Mancozeb technical employed in the manufacture 
of the material shall conform to IS 8707 and tricyclazole 
technical shall conform to IS 15982. 


3.2 Physical 


The material shall comply with 
requirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4. 


the physical 


3.2.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of yellow powder free 
from hard lumps and shall wet readily on mixing with 
water providing a suspension suitable for use as spray. 


3.2.2 Sieving Requirement 


When determined by the method specified in 11.1 
of IS 6940, the amount of material passing through 
75 micron IS sieve | see IS 460 (Part 1) ], should not be 
less than 98 percent by mass. 


3.2.3 Suspensibility 


The suspensibility should be not less than 75 percent 
by mass, when tested by the method specified in 11.2 
of IS 6940. 


3.2.4 Wettability 


The time when the whole material gets completely 
submerged in water should not exceed 120 s when 
tested by the method specified in 11.4 of IS 6940. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall also comply with chemical 
requirements specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


3.3.1 Tricyclazole and Mancozeb Content 


When determined by the method prescribed in Annex 
A for tricyclazole content and IS 8707 for mancozeb 
content, the observed tricyclazole content, in percent, 
(w/w) and mancozeb content, in percent (w/w), of 
any of the samples shall not differ from the declared 
nominal value by more than the percent tolerance limits 
indicated below : 


Nominal Value, Tolerance Limits, 


Percent Percent of the Nominal 
Value 
Up to 9 +10 
-5 
Above 9 and below 50 +5 
50 and above eS 
-3 


IS 16917 : 2018 


3.3.2 Acidity or Alkalinity 
When tested by the method specified in 11.3 of IS 6940, 


the acidity (as H,SO,) or alkalinity (as NaOH) of the 
material shall be 0.5 percent by mass, Max. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in trilaminated pouches 
comprising of PET/Aluminium foil/LDPE. The 
pouches shall be heat sealed to make it leak proof 
and pilfer proof. The trilaminated pouches up to 
1 kg capacity shall be inserted in duplex board up to 
250 g and 3 ply CFB E — flute carton for 500 g 
and 1 kg as secondary pack. All types of containers 
shall further be packed in Corrugated fiberboard 
boxes as per IS 2771 (Part 1). The container shall also 
comply with the general requirements specified in 
IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The container shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following information in addition to the information as 
is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules 
framed thereunder: 


a) Name ofthe material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal tricyclazole and mancozeb content, 
percent (m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the Insecticides 
Act, 1968, and Rules framed thereunder; and 


j) Any other information required under the Legal 
Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 
and the Rules and regulations made thereunder. The 
details of the conditions under which the licence for use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


6 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material in bulk quantity 
and/or the retail pack of the formulated product is/ 
are offered for inspection, representative sample of 
the material shall be drawn and tested as prescribed 
in IS 10627 and if tested within 90 days of its date of 
manufacture, the criteria for conformity shall be that 
the contents, in percent (m/m), shall not be less than the 
declared nominal value. The upper limit for conformity 
shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1. 


When the material is offered for inspection after 
90 days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done 
as prescribed in IS 10627. However, the criteria for 
conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the 
limits of tolerances, as applicable on the declared 
nominal value as given under 3.3.1. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred to 
in 3.2.2 to 3.2.4, 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — “Pure chemicals” shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 16917 : 2018 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 3.3.1) 


DETERMINATION OF TRICYCLAZOLE CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Tricyclazole content is determined by gas liquid 
chromatograph (GLC) with flame ionization detector 
(FID) using internal standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Gas Liquid Chromatograph (GLC) 


A gas chromatograph equipped with flame ionization 
detector (FID) and coupled to chromatography software 
and printer is used for this determination. 


Instrument GLC with FID 

Column Glass, length 2.0 m, ID 2.5 mm, 
packed with 3 percent OV-17 on 
Chromosorb WHP, 80 / 100 mesh 

Flow rate Nitrogen 30 ml/min, Hydrogen 


30 ml/min, Air 300 ml/min 
20 ul 
Oven temperature : 230°C 


Injection volume 

Temperatures 
Injector temperature : 250°C 
Detector temperature : 280°C 

A-2.2 Analytical Balance 

A-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 10 ul capacity 

A-2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 

A-2.5 Standard Glassware 


A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Chloroform — AR grade, or equivalent 


A-3.2 Internal Standard, Dioctyl Phthalate — AR 
grade, or equivalent 


A-3.3 Tricyclazole Reference Standard — Of known 
purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard 


Weigh accurately about 6.0 g of dioctyl phthalate into 
a 250 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in chloroform and 
make up the volume up to the mark with chloroform. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately about 0.1 g of tricyclazole reference 
standard of known purity into a 25 ml volumetric flask. 


Add 5 ml of the internal standard solution (see B-4.1), 
sonicate and make up to the mark with chloroform. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh 0.55 g tricyclazole + mancozeb WP sample into 
25 ml volumetric flask. Add 10 ml chloroform, shake 
well and filter. Add 5 ml chloroform again, shake well 
and filter. Add 5 ml chloroform and pool all filtrate in 
another 25 ml volumetric flask. Now add 5 ml internal 
standard (see A-4.1), sonicate and make up the volume 
with chloroform. Shake well to homogenize and inject. 


A-4.4 Estimation 


Inject 1 pl standard solution until the internal standard 
/ reference substance area quotients of two successive 
chromatograms do not deviate from each other by 
more than 2 percent. Then use the following injection 
sequence: 


where, 
C = Standard Solution, and 
S = Sample solution (1, 2, ....... ,n) 


From the chromatograms of the standard solution and 
sample solution, measure the peak areas of the internal 
standard and Tricyclazole peaks, and compute the 
percentage of the Tricyclazole as given in A-6. 


A-5 RETENTION TIME (GUIDE VALUES) 


A-5.1 Tricyclazole ~ 3.5 min 


A-5.2 Dioctyl Phthalate (Internal Standard) =% 
8.0 min 


A-5.3 Total Run Time — 12 min. 


A-5.4 A typical GC chromatogram of tricyclazole with 
internal standard is given in Fig. 1.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
